newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH KPW HEAD SEES SECURITIES BILL VOTE IN Q2.
newsitem.headline: POLISH KPW HEAD SEES SECURITIES BILL VOTE IN Q2.

text.p: A bill to help adjust Poland's securities law to international norms might be ready for a final parliamentary vote within three months, the head of the Polish Securities Commission (KPW) said on Thursday.
Jacek Socha told a news conference that both houses of parliament, after the work of sub-committees, might be ready to vote on the bill in three to four months.

"It's a large legal act but to a large degree, about 65 to 75 percent, it's based on the current law...so it seems there shouldn't be any problems and...in the next three months the law could be brought to vote," Socha said.
Last month the government sent the bill to the lower house, which sent it to parliamentary committees.

Analysts say the law would create a legal framework for the introduction of new instruments such as futures and options and help Polish brokerages develop by granting them the right to provide investment-bank-type services.
